simple: Your body now follows the profile you load: load a profile and within a couple of seconds you become that profile's chef (it never switched before).

notes: Chef detection: the texture pieces had to have 20 distinct byte values in 48 bytes; the chef textures reach at most 17, so no piece was ever chosen ('0 male and 0 female pieces' in every log). Now the 6 most detailed 64-byte pieces per chef that the other chef's texture lacks; one pass over RSX local memory every 2 s with an 8-byte lookup per aligned block; a chef wins with 2+ pieces and 2 more than the other.

Lobby parts: a mesh part is its block (material id 0x198 before its first segment) plus every drawn segment (attribute block size > 0) up to the next block; shadow copies are skipped. Before, two segments per part were assumed, so in Stuffolini, Chez Haute and the burger joint every object after the first big part took another object's place and material.

Lobby: segments with non-finite or out-of-range positions are dropped; overlay/decal/shadow names skipped; standing spot near the median of the dining tables when the layout names them, floor height taken near them.
Lobby scale 0.9; seated (or floor unknown): restaurant floor 1.6 m below the eyes at board placement.

simple: New VR lobby: around the menus you now stand inside one of the game's own restaurants, a different one each time you start (Gravy Chug, El Fuego, Stuffolini, Chez Haute, Kung Fusion or the burger joint).

Until it has loaded (well under a second), you see the old diner.
notes: Lobby (OrderUpVR_lobby.inl): reads the restaurant package in Chef.wad: the scene model (material records found by their ffffcd/0xfc signature, node table by its count + 12 x 0xbe + 0xab filler, Edge segments decoded with the game's SPU decoder; vertex stream 24 or 36 bytes per vertex as the segment header gives), the layout file (name, position, quaternion, scale per node; node hash = ~crc32(lowercase name)), the material files (picture size, DXT1/DXT5, image id) and the picture package that holds most of the images.

Skipped: sky, exterior, street, buildings and the decal overlays (AOFakery, Downgrade stains). Opaque, cut-out (DXT5), see-through and glow (flag 0x80) batches; RGBA textures with mipmaps; anisotropic wrap sampling; vertex colours as baked light.

Where you stand: a 20 cm floor grid (floor below, ceiling above, nothing from 12 cm to 1.9 m), within 10 m of the restaurant's median, among roomy spots the one with the longest free view; the menu board hangs in that view.
Dev tools: --ouvr-lobby-test <usrdir> <out> (rebuilds all six and dumps them), --ouvr-edge-dump <usrdir> <model> <out>.

A standing mirror in the diner lobby, to your front left: look at yourself as the chef, wave, and move around.

How it works: the game stores its characters for the PS3's SPU processors (Sony Edge compressed geometry). The mod runs the game's own SPU decoder in a small interpreter to rebuild the model, so it matches the game exactly.
Fixed the black right eye in cutscenes (the waiter taking orders): there the game shows each picture twice, and both copies went to the left eye. Eyes now take turns on every new picture.
The placeholder body and the button shapes on your hands are gone: you see your hands only, until the game's own male and female chef models are in (being worked on).

The kitchen has walls: the stick cannot take you more than 1 m from your spot, and walking further for real darkens the edges of your view.
The order tickets and the rest of the HUD are never nearer than the kitchen itself, so they no longer end up in your way when you lean or walk in.
In the restaurant (things far away), you point with a ray from your hand instead of having to cover things with it.
The launcher no longer opens the long guide after an update; it just says it updated. The guide is still under Help.

The kitchen is now a real place around you. When the game moves its camera to another station, the kitchen no longer slides with it: it stays still in your room, and the new station appears where it really is. The mod measures the camera's motion from the kitchen itself every frame (Settings > VR comfort and body > Kitchen world; 'Follows the game camera' is the old behaviour).

Turn to change station: press A or B once in the kitchen so the mod learns which way they go, then just turn your head toward the next station and the game moves there (Look to change station, on by default). A and B keep working as before.
Reaching for things follows the room too, so your hand still lands on the burger after a station change.

Menus are now a menu board in a diner: checkered floor, tiled walls, counters with a grill and a fryer, and warm lamps around you, with a sign that welcomes first-time chefs. Point with your hand and pull the trigger to choose.
Still includes the camera research from 0.8.1. After a session, press Collect logs and attach the zip to the LogsRecordDump issue: the new room log lines show how well the kitchen stays still.

Everything from 0.8.0, plus the first step to steering the game's own camera: while you play in the kitchen or the restaurant, the mod finds where the game keeps its camera (its direction and its field of view) in the PS3's memory.

It searches for the camera in every common form: rotation matrices, direction vectors, quaternions, yaw and pitch angles in radians or degrees, and ten forms of the field of view. It keeps only the places that follow the camera when it moves between stations.

It confirms each one by changing it for a split second while the view is still and watching whether the picture reacts; field-of-view values are tested in groups and narrowed down by halves. You may notice a tiny twitch now and then; the value is put back at once.

It also saves a compact copy of the game memory that changed when the camera moved, so if the camera is stored in a form nobody predicted, it can still be found from that copy without another play session.
After a session of a few minutes in the kitchen (let the camera move between stations at least once), press Collect logs and attach the zip to the LogsRecordDump issue as before.

Fixed the small square: the 3D view now fills the restaurant and kitchen again. 0.7.0 read the wrong drawing slot for where the game draws its 3D scene, so the picture the game copies onto the screen (with its blue sky) was mistaken for the HUD and shrunk onto a panel 4 metres away.

Scenery pictures the game draws behind the 3D world (like the sky) now sit far away behind everything, and the HUD, order tickets and menus float at a comfortable reading distance (1.5 m, adjustable).

Fixed the double image: each eye now always shows the picture that was drawn for that eye, from where your head was at that moment. In 0.6.0 the game showed a picture one step older than the mod expected, so the eyes and head positions were mixed up, which made the view double and wobbly.
Your own body: a chef with white jacket, apron, arms and legs. Look down and you see yourself; the arms follow your hands naturally (elbows bend on their own).

Real hands instead of the laser inside the game: they follow the controllers and close their fingers when you squeeze GRIP (middle, ring and little finger) and the TRIGGER (index finger). The game's pointer is wherever your hand covers something, so you reach for the burger instead of aiming at it.

Start-up 'press square' screen: a hint card explains it is the X button on the left controller, and pulling the TRIGGER works too, until the game has done it once.
The order tickets, timers, pop-ups and the pause menu are no longer stuck to the edges of your view: they sit in the world in front of you, where the game shows them.
The empty space the game never draws (it was sky blue) is now a calm dark room instead.
Right stick up/down inside the game moves you lower or higher (the restaurant camera stood too high). It is remembered.
Smoother headset motion: picture conversion moved off the headset's own thread, and the game renders at 2x instead of 3x resolution to keep frames coming steadily.
Still to come: the game itself only draws what its own camera sees, so behind and far to the sides there is no restaurant to show.

True VR, first step: in the kitchen and the restaurant you are now inside the game in 3D instead of in front of a screen. The game is drawn separately for each eye from where your head really is, so you get real depth, can look around and lean in. Built from the camera data you collected: the mod recognises the game's camera in every 3D draw and re-renders it from your eyes.
The game's own horizon is levelled with the real one (the kitchen camera looks down at the counter, so you look down at it too, like a real cook) and the scale matches the real world.
Move with the left stick (walks where you look) and turn with the right stick in 30 degree steps. Left stick click recentres you at the game's camera.
The game's HUD, order tickets and pop-ups are placed in the world in front of you instead of being glued to your face, at the distance of the things you work on.
Pointing works in 3D: aim at things in the scene; the laser and ring follow into the scene.

Menus and loading screens switch to the big screen by themselves. Hold the left stick click for 1 second to switch between 3D and the big screen at any time (remembered for next time), for example if something looks wrong.
The How to play guide and the Controls card in the headset are updated with the new controls, and the launcher shows the guide again once.
Not yet tried in a headset. If 3D looks wrong, switch to the big screen (hold left stick click), then press Collect logs after the session and send the zip.

Smoother pointer: removed the hand movement that 0.4.0 added to the pointer while holding GRIP (it made dragging feel sometimes fast, sometimes slow) and added light smoothing that steadies hand tremor without adding delay. Flicks still work through the controller's rotation and speed.
New laser and cursor: a beam from your hand and a ring where it hits the screen, drawn directly by the headset, so you see exactly where you point without waiting for the game.

First-time introduction: the launcher shows a How to play guide after installing (and from the new ? button), and the headset shows a Controls card next to the screen during your first session. Hold Left MENU for 2 seconds to bring it back at any time.
Loading screen: the 'first start' explanation now appears only when the game really prepares after an install or update. Normal starts just show Loading with a progress bar and controller tips.
Groundwork for true VR (see docs/TRUE_VR_PLAN.md): this version quietly records the game's camera data while you play. After a session that reaches the kitchen, press Collect logs and send the zip.
Controls swapped as in most VR games: GRIP now grabs and holds (the game's T button), TRIGGER selects and confirms (the Move button).

Motion support: the Quest controller's real movement and rotation are now sent to the game the way a PlayStation Move reports them (rotation, speed, acceleration, spin and its motion sensors). Motion actions such as flipping a burger should now work with a real flick: hold GRIP on the item, then flick your wrist up and over in a half circle.

Backup for motion actions: while holding GRIP, flick the thumbstick of the same hand up. This plays a clean flip motion for you, in case your own flick is not recognised. (While holding GRIP the thumbsticks no longer move or resize the screen.)

First start loading: the headset now shows RPCS3's real preparation progress with a progress bar, the percentage, what is being prepared and the time left, instead of a counting timer. The launcher shows the same progress bar.

Pointing at the screen works as before. Not yet tested in the real game: whether the game accepts every motion the tutorial asks for. If a motion action does not work, collect logs right after trying it and send them.

Fixed: 0.3.0 showed "RPCS3: Fatal Error - the module msvcp140.dll was incorrectly installed" when pressing Play. RPCS3 refuses to run with its own copy of Microsoft's Visual C++ files, so the mod no longer includes them, and updating removes the ones 0.3.0 left behind.

Instead, the launcher checks that Microsoft's Visual C++ Runtime is installed in Windows. If it is missing or too old, it offers to download and install the official package from Microsoft (it only runs it after checking Microsoft's digital signature).
Updates now remove any program files a new version no longer uses, so nothing outdated is left behind.
The VR part is unchanged and still needs its first test on a real headset.

New launcher: redesigned from scratch with a modern look, smooth animations and rounded corners. It has a step-by-step setup that finds your folders by itself, a live status panel, a settings page and notifications. It also snaps and minimizes like a normal Windows app.

Fixed: the mod relied on Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime already being on the PC. It now ships its own copy, so it works on a fresh Windows install. Every release is now checked automatically for files that normal PCs might not have.
New: Order Up VR appears in Windows' Settings > Apps > Installed apps, and can be uninstalled from there or from the launcher.

New: uninstalling asks whether to keep your settings and game cache for a quick reinstall later, or remove everything. A full uninstall leaves nothing behind. Your own RPCS3, firmware, saves and game files are never touched.
Only one launcher window opens at a time; starting it again brings the open one to the front.
While playing, the launcher minimizes itself and comes back when the game closes (you can turn this off in Settings).
The VR part is unchanged from 0.2.0 and still needs its first test on a real headset.

Fixed: pressing Play gave a black headset and no game window (only the boot music played). The mod's game settings switched on a Vulkan debugging option that only works on PCs with the Vulkan SDK installed, so on normal PCs the game's graphics never started. That option is now off, and the mod build ignores it if it is ever switched on again.
The mod now ships only the settings it needs (Vulkan renderer, Move emulation, no pausing when the window loses focus). Everything else uses your own RPCS3 settings.

New: a status panel in the headset while the game starts, instead of a black screen. It also tells you when the game window on the PC is minimized, because the headset can only show the game while that window is open.

New: after you press Play the launcher shows what is happening: game starting, game window open with FPS, VR runtime and headset state. It brings the game window to the front and tells you if the game closes or RPCS3 shows an error.
Collect logs now includes the full RPCS3 log again (it was switched off), the launcher's own notes from the last start, and opens the folder with the zip so you can send it.
Not yet tested on a real Quest 3. Real 3D depth and a head-tracked camera are still to come.
First test build.
The game appears on a large virtual screen in the headset (checked in a headset simulator, not yet in a real Quest 3).
The VR controller you aim at the screen is the game's PlayStation Move pointer. The hand that pulls its trigger becomes the pointing hand.
Calibration screen: point at the middle of the screen and press X (the game's Square), then squeeze the grip to continue.
Buttons: trigger = T, grip = Move, A/B/X/Y = Cross/Circle/Square/Triangle, left menu = START, right stick click = SELECT.
Screen: left stick click recentres it, right stick up/down moves it nearer or farther, left stick up/down resizes it.
Not done yet: real 3D depth and head-tracked camera. The tutorial has not been played through in Move mode.
